blocking.source_evidence: rendering-rules.md:55 pins the string: "Finished traversal with n not T: `collected n / reported T (mismatch)`." acceptance-tests.md:41 (T47) says mismatch notes "render per `rendering-rules.md`", so T47's mismatch part has a pinned target today.
blocking.why_blocking: False claim against the spec. It hands a pinned string to the UX step to reinvent, and it declares part of a spec test (T47) pending when the spec makes it runnable now. That weakens a CAP-4 success criterion.
blocking.fix: Replace the sentence with: a finished traversal where n differs from T renders `collected n / reported T (mismatch)` (rendering-rules.md), pinned by T47. Remove 'the UX step sets it' and 'stays pending'.

blocking.prd_location: §3 Glossary, PARTIAL / STALE / FAILED row, prd.md:88
blocking.claim: PARTIAL is defined as "fewer rows collected than reported".
blocking.source_evidence: rendering-rules.md:55: PARTIAL applies when "`page.hasMore` is still true at the call cap", or when `workers=[]` with T above 0 (`PARTIAL (empty page k)`); a finished traversal with n not equal to T is `(mismatch)`, not PARTIAL. adapter-contract.md:15: the cursor guard "marks the view PARTIAL when the per-cycle cap stops it". unverified-register.md:41 and PRD K3 (prd.md:362) note `page.total` may include historical dispatches, so collected < reported can happen on a complete read.
blocking.why_blocking: Wrong behaviour. Implementing the PRD definition would show PARTIAL whenever collected < reported, including complete traversals where `page.total` counts historical dispatches. The spec says those cases are mismatch, not PARTIAL, so the header would routinely misstate completeness. That is the honesty property CAP-4 exists to protect.
blocking.fix: Define PARTIAL as in rendering-rules.md:55: paging stopped at the 5-call cap while `page.hasMore` was still true, or an empty page with T above 0. Add a separate glossary entry for mismatch: traversal finished, but n is not T.
